findings.evidence: "Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing. The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes." (line 21)
findings.fix: Separate employee-facing instructions from administrative descriptions into distinct sections or clearly label each instruction with the role it addresses (e.g., "Manager: Review the request..."; "Employee: Once your manager signs...").
findings.violation: The document addresses employees, managers, and finance/payroll staff in the same sections without clear audience separation. Instructions for employees ("Employees start a stipend request") are interleaved with descriptions of what managers do ("once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line"), leaving readers unsure which instructions apply to them.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: Special Cases heading names special cases, but content is: "The IT asset group updates the equipment catalog after every open enrollment period. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit." This is routine maintenance, not a special case. Program Coordination: "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter." The first sentence establishes coordination as the topic; the next three sentences are audit, federal guidance, and budget - three unrelated tangents.
findings.fix: Special Cases: Either rename the section to match content (e.g., "Catalog Updates") or move the content elsewhere and define what special cases actually apply. Program Coordination: Remove the three unrelated sentences (audit, federal guidance, coffee budget). Keep only: "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout."
findings.violation: Section headings do not match content or sections lack a unifying theme. Special Cases describes routine catalog updates after enrollment, not special cases. Program Coordination starts with coordination but then lists audit, federal guidance, and coffee budget - unrelated topics that prevent a reader from identifying the section's theme.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears." (lines 51 - 53: subjects shift from employee to Finance to Payroll to employee to manager to employee). "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter." (line 65: subjects jump from benefits team to audit to guidance to budget with no transitions).
findings.fix: Terminology Notes: Group sentences by actor (employee actions together, Finance actions together, Payroll actions together) with transitions between groups. Program Coordination: Remove the three unrelated sentences (audit, federal guidance, coffee budget) as they belong in a different document or section.
findings.violation: Rapid subject shifts within paragraphs break cohesion. Terminology Notes cycles through employee → Finance → Payroll → manager → employee without transitions. Program Coordination jumps from coordination topic to three unrelated topics (audit, federal guidance, coffee budget) with no logical connection.

findings.evidence: Reimbursement Amounts is section 6, positioned after "How to Apply" (section 3), "Approval Timeline" (section 4), and "Required Documentation" (section 5). The section states: "The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year." (line 39)
findings.fix: Move Reimbursement Amounts to immediately after Eligibility, before How to Apply, so readers can assess the benefit level early.
findings.violation: Reimbursement Amounts appears too late in the document. Readers need to know the stipend amount early to decide whether to pursue the application, but this information comes after How to Apply, Approval Timeline, and Required Documentation, adding unnecessary reordering.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: "Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing." (line 21: subject is "the stipend request" instead of "Finance" or "the system"). "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives." (line 29: subject is "An incomplete request" instead of naming who pauses it). "The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year." (line 39: subject is "The stipend" instead of "Finance" or "the program").
findings.fix: Replace abstract subjects with real actors: "Finance moves the stipend request to final processing"; "An incomplete request causes a pause in the timeline"; "The program provides up to 500 dollars per benefit year."
findings.location: How to Apply, line 21; Approval Timeline, line 29; Reimbursement Amounts, line 39
findings.violation: Three sentences use abstract subjects (requests, stipends) instead of naming the real actors (Finance, Payroll, managers). Readers must infer who performs the action rather than being told directly.
